narrative:
The model estimated a 48% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. This is close to an even chance of repayment problems, and it fell on the denial side of the bank’s cutoff, so the application was not approved.

The strongest reason was your checking account status: it is recorded as overdrawn, below zero DM. This was the most influential factor and it pushed the prediction toward bad credit. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% had this status, while most had no negative balance, so it stood out as a warning sign. Two other important factors worked in your favor. The amount you requested, 2406 DM, is below the approved applicants’ average of about 3019 DM, so the smaller requested exposure helped your case. Your four-to-seven years of employment also counted as a favorable signal, suggesting some income stability. Even so, those positive factors were not enough to offset the concern raised by the overdrawn account.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing the checking account back to a positive balance and keeping it there for several months before reapplying. Avoid overdrafts and other signs of cash-flow strain. You could also ask the bank what balance or waiting period they would consider acceptable, and whether adding a guarantor or building savings would strengthen a future application. Reapplying after these steps gives the bank a clearer picture of stable finances.
